<a id="entry-t-000001"></a>
## t

*n.* 1. **脫氧胸苷酸** — one of the four nucleotides used in building DNA; all four nucleotides have a common phosphate group and a sugar (ribose)
2. **公噸** — a unit of weight equivalent to 1000 kilograms
3. a base found in DNA (but not in RNA) and derived from pyrimidine; pairs with adenine
4. the 20th letter of the Roman alphabet
5. thyroid hormone similar to thyroxine but with one less iodine atom per molecule and produced in smaller quantity; exerts the same biological effects as thyroxine but is more potent and briefer
6. hormone produced by the thyroid glands to regulate metabolism by controlling the rate of oxidation in cells
*“thyroxine is 65% iodine”*

## tack

*v.* 1. **搶風航行, 搶風調向, 搶風轉變航向** — turn into the wind

*“append a charm to the necklace”*

5. (nautical) the act of changing tack

*n.* 1. *(uncountable)* **機智 /機智, 輕重感 /輕重感, 分寸感, 禮貌 /禮貌** — Sensitive mental touch; special skill or faculty; keen perception or discernment; ready power of appreciating and doing what is required by circumstances; the ability to say the right thing and avoid statements that will give offence or pain even if true.
2. consideration in dealing with others and avoiding giving offense

<a id="entry-t-000082"></a>
## tactful

*adj.* 1. **言行得體+的** — having or showing a sense of what is fitting and considerate in dealing with others
*“she was tactful enough not to shatter his illusion”*
*“a tactful remark eased her embarrassment”*
2. showing skill and sensitivity in dealing with people
*“by diplomatic conduct he avoided antagonizing anyone”*
*“a tactful way of correcting someone”*

<a id="entry-t-000083"></a>

3. **戰術 /戰術** — A maneuver used against an enemy.

<a id="entry-t-000086"></a>

*v.* 1. **實行, 採取, 執行** — carry out

*“It took three hours to get to work this morning”*
*“This event occupied a very short time”*

*“We lead him to our chief”*
*“can you take me to the main entrance?”*

*“His voice took on a sad tone”*

*“Bring me the box from the other room”*

*“We are taking an orphan from Romania”*
*“I'll take three salmon steaks”*

## taste

**發音：** /teɪst/
*v.* 1. **有某種味道** — have flavor; taste of something
2. **品嚐, 嘗** — perceive by the sense of taste
*“Can you taste the garlic?”*
3. **品嚐, 辨味, 嘗, 嘗味** — take a sample of
*“Try these new crackers”*
*“Sample the regional dishes”*
4. *(copulative, intransitive)* **味道** — To have a taste; to excite a particular sensation by which flavor is distinguished.
5. **品味, 嘗, 嘗味, 品嚐** — distinguish flavors
*“We tasted wines last night”*
6. *(transitive)* **嘗味 /嘗味, 嘗 /嘗, 品嘗 /品嚐** — To sample the flavor of something orally.
*n.* 1. **偏好, 愛好, 偏愛, 喜愛, 嗜好** — a strong liking
*“my own preference is for good literature”*
*“the Irish have a penchant for blarney”*
2. *(countable, uncountable)* **味道, 味兒 /味兒, 氣味 /氣味, 味覺 /味覺** — One of the sensations produced by the tongue in response to certain chemicals; the quality of giving this sensation.
3. *(countable, uncountable)* **品味** — A person's implicit set of preferences, especially esthetic, though also culinary, sartorial, etc.
4. **味覺, 味道, 味兒, 氣味** — the faculty of distinguishing sweet, sour, bitter, and salty properties in the mouth
*“his cold deprived him of his sense of taste”*
5. the sensation that results when taste buds in the tongue and throat convey information about the chemical composition of a soluble stimulus
*“the candy left him with a bad taste”*
*“the melon had a delicious taste”*
6. delicate discrimination (especially of aesthetic values)
*“arrogance and lack of taste contributed to his rapid success”*
*“to ask at that particular time was the ultimate in bad taste”*

## tax

**發音：** /tæks/

*v.* 1. **課以稅** — levy a tax on
*“The State taxes alcohol heavily”*
*“Clothing is not taxed in our state”*

3. **評判, 評定, 評估** — set or determine the amount of (a payment such as a fine)
4. use to the limit
*“you are taxing my patience”*
5. make a charge against or accuse
*“They taxed him failure to appear in court”*

## theory

**發音：** /ˈθɪə.ɹi/
*n.* 1. **假說, 理論, 論** — a tentative insight into the natural world; a concept that is not yet verified but that if true would explain certain facts or phenomena
*“a scientific hypothesis that survives experimental testing becomes a scientific theory”*
*“he proposed a fresh theory of alkalis that later was accepted in chemical practices”*
2. *(countable, uncountable)* **理論 /理論, 學說 /學說** — A coherent statement or set of ideas that explains observed facts or phenomena and correctly predicts new facts or phenomena not previously observed, or which sets out the laws and principles of something known or observed; a hypothesis confirmed by observation, experiment etc.
3. *(countable, uncountable)* **理論 /理論, 學說 /學說** — A field of study attempting to exhaustively describe a particular class of constructs.
4. *(countable)* **定理** — A set of axioms together with all statements derivable from them; or, a set of statements which are deductively closed. Equivalently, a formal language plus a set of axioms (from which can then be derived theorems). The statements may be required to all be bound (i.e., to have no free variables).
5. *(countable, informal, uncountable)* **理論 /理論** — A hypothesis or conjecture.
6. a well-substantiated explanation of some aspect of the natural world; an organized system of accepted knowledge that applies in a variety of circumstances to explain a specific set of phenomena
*“theories can incorporate facts and laws and tested hypotheses”*
*“true in fact and theory”*

<a id="entry-t-001591"></a>

## think

*v.* 1. **想, 看待, 認為, 以為, 相信** — judge or regard; look upon; judge
*“I think he is very smart”*
*“I believe her to be very smart”*
2. **思索, 思考, 想** — use or exercise the mind or one's power of reason in order to make inferences, decisions, or arrive at a solution or judgments
*“I've been thinking all day and getting nowhere”*
3. **回憶, 回想, 憶起, 想起, 記得** — recall knowledge from memory; have a recollection
*“I can't remember saying any such thing”*
*“I can't think what her last name was”*
4. expect, believe, or suppose
*“I imagine she earned a lot of money with her new novel”*
*“I thought to find her in a bad state”*
5. imagine or visualize
*“Just think--you could be rich one day!”*
*“Think what a scene it must have been!”*
6. focus one's attention on a certain state
*“Think big”*
*“think thin”*

## tick

*“The clock ticked away”*

*“the clocks were ticking”*
*“the grandfather clock beat midnight”*
3. **打勾** — To make a clicking noise similar to the movement of the hands of an analog clock.
4. **核對** — put a check mark on or near or next to
*“Please check each name on the list”*
*“tick off the items”*
5. sew
*“tick a mattress”*

## time

**發音：** /taɪm/
*n.* 1. **時間** — a period of time considered as a resource under your control and sufficient to accomplish something
*“take time to smell the roses”*
*“I didn't have time to finish”*
2. **適當時機** — a suitable moment
*“it is time to go”*
3. **時候, 時刻, 時鐘時間, 時間** — a reading of a point in time as given by a clock
*“do you know what time it is?”*
*“the time is 10 o'clock”*
4. **刑期** — the period of time a prisoner is imprisoned
*“he served a prison term of 15 months”*
*“his sentence was 5 to 10 years”*
5. an instance or single occasion for some event
*“this time he succeeded”*
*“he called four times”*
6. an indefinite period (usually marked by specific attributes or activities)
*“he waited a long time”*
*“the time of year for planting”*
*v.* 1. **為確定時間, 計時** — measure the time or duration of an event or action or the person who performs an action in a certain period of time
*“he clocked the runners”*
2. **計時 /計時** — To measure, as in music or harmony.
3. assign a time for an activity or event
*“The candidate carefully timed his appearance at the disaster scene”*
4. set the speed, duration, or execution of
*“we time the process to manufacture our cars very precisely”*
5. regulate or set the time of
*“time the clock”*
6. adjust so that a force is applied and an action occurs at the desired time
*“The good player times his swing so as to hit the ball squarely”*

*“he held the title for two years”*

*“They styled their nation `The Confederate States'”*

## tone

**發音：** /ˈtəʊn/
*n.* 1. **聲調, 聲音的腔調, 腔調, 語調, 語氣** — the quality of a person's voice
*“he began in a conversational tone”*
*“he spoke in a nervous tone of voice”*
2. **感覺, 風氣, 情緒, 氣氛, 心情** — the general atmosphere of a place or situation and the effect that it has on people
*“the feel of the city excited him”*
*“a clergyman improved the tone of the meeting”*
3. **音符** — a notation representing the pitch and duration of a musical sound
*“the singer held the note too long”*
4. **全音** — (in the diatonic scale) An interval of a major second.
5. **聲調 /聲調, 聲 /聲, 四聲 /四聲** — The pitch of a word's sound that distinguishes a difference in meaning, as for example in Chinese.
6. **強壯, 肌肉彈性, 肌肉的彈性** — the elastic tension of living muscles, arteries, etc. that facilitate response to stimuli
*“the doctor tested my tonicity”*
*v.* 1. utter monotonously and repetitively and rhythmically
*“The students chanted the same slogan over and over again”*
2. vary the pitch of one's speech
3. change the color or tone of
*“tone a negative”*
4. change to a color image
*“tone a photographic image”*
5. give a healthy elasticity to
*“Let's tone our muscles”*

## trail

**發音：** /tɹeɪl/
*v.* 1. **落後於, 拖拉, 落後, 遲緩, 拖** — to lag or linger behind
*“But in so many other areas we still are dragging”*
2. **奔逐, 循路而行, 追逐, 逐, 追** — go after with the intent to catch
*“The policeman chased the mugger down the alley”*
*“the dog chased the rabbit”*
3. *(transitive)* **跟蹤, 追蹤** — To follow behind (someone or something); to tail (someone or something).
4. **慢吞吞地走, 拖沓行走** — move, proceed, or walk draggingly or slowly
*“John trailed behind his class mates”*
*“The Mercedes trailed behind the horse cart”*
5. hang down so as to drag along the ground
*“The bride's veiled trailed along the ground”*
6. drag loosely along a surface; allow to sweep the ground
*“The toddler was trailing his pants”*
*“She trained her long scarf behind her”*
*n.* 1. **循路而行, 線索, 追蹤** — evidence pointing to a possible solution
*“the police are following a promising lead”*
*“the trail led straight to the perpetrator”*
2. **足跡 /足跡, 蹤跡 /蹤跡, 痕跡 /痕跡** — The track or indication marking the route followed by something that has passed, such as the footprints of animal on land or the contrail of an airplane in the sky.
3. **路徑 /路徑, 小徑 /小徑, 山道** — A route for travel over land, especially a narrow, unpaved pathway for use by hikers, horseback riders, etc.
4. a track or mark left by something that has passed
*“there as a trail of blood”*
*“a tear left its trail on her cheek”*
5. a path or track roughly blazed through wild or hilly country

2. *(US)* **預告 /預告, 預告片 /預告片** — A preview of a film, video game or TV show.
3. someone who takes more time than necessary; someone who lags behind
4. an advertisement consisting of short scenes from a motion picture that will appear in the near future
5. a large transport conveyance designed to be pulled by a truck or tractor
6. a wheeled vehicle that can be pulled by a car or truck and is equipped for occupancy

<a id="entry-t-003173"></a>
## train

*n.* 1. **列車, 火車** — public transport provided by a line of railway cars coupled together and drawn by a locomotive
*“express trains don't stop at Princeton Junction”*
2. **傳動系, 檔, 齒輪裝置, 傳動裝置** — wheelwork consisting of a connected set of rotating gears by which force is transmitted or motion or torque is changed
*“the fool got his tie caught in the geartrain”*
3. a sequentially ordered set of things or events or ideas in which each successive member is related to the preceding
*“a string of islands”*
*“train of mourners”*
4. a procession (of wagons or mules or camels) traveling together in single file
*“we were part of a caravan of almost a thousand camels”*
*“they joined the wagon train for safety”*
5. a series of consequences wrought by an event
*“it led to a train of disasters”*
6. piece of cloth forming the long back section of a gown that is drawn along the floor
*“the bride's train was carried by her two young nephews”*
*v.* 1. **培訓, 訓練, 制訂, 培養** — create by training and teaching
*“The old master is training world-class violinists”*
*“we develop the leaders for the future”*
2. **教訓, 訓導, 訓服, 訓誡, 訓練** — develop (children's) behavior by instruction and practice; especially to teach self-control
*“Parents must discipline their children”*
*“Is this dog trained?”*
3. **專門培訓, 鍛鍊, 訓練, 培養** — educate for a future role or function
*“He is grooming his son to become his successor”*
*“The prince was prepared to become King one day”*
4. **磨鍊, 訓練, 教育, 培養** — teach or refine to be discriminative in taste or judgment
*“Cultivate your musical taste”*
*“Train your tastebuds”*
5. **對準, 瞄準** — point or cause to go (blows, weapons, or objects such as photographic equipment) towards
*“Please don't aim at your little brother!”*
*“He trained his gun on the burglar”*
6. **訓煉, 輔導** — teach and supervise (someone); act as a trainer or coach (to), as in sports
*“He is training our Olympic team”*
*“She is coaching the crew”*

*n.* 1. **庫存, 資金, 基金, 經費** — the funds of a government or institution or individual
2. **金庫 /金庫** — A place where treasure is stored safely.
3. **國庫 /國庫** — A place where state or royal money and valuables are stored.
4. **國庫券** — negotiable debt obligations of the United States government which guarantees that interest and principal payments will be paid on time
5. **寶庫 /寶庫** — A collection of artistic or literary works.
6. the government department responsible for collecting and managing and spending public revenues

<a id="entry-t-003466"></a>
## Treasury bill

*n.* 1. **國庫券 /國庫券** — A government obligation, sold at a discount, maturing in one year or less, and pay no interest prior to maturity.

<a id="entry-t-003467"></a>
## treasury bill

*n.* 1. **短期國庫券** — a short-term obligation that is not interest-bearing (it is purchased at a discount); can be traded on a discount basis for 91 days

<a id="entry-t-003468"></a>
## treasury bond

*n.* 1. **長期國庫券** — a debt instrument with maturities of 10 years or longer

<a id="entry-t-003469"></a>

<a id="entry-t-003470"></a>

## treat

**發音：** /tɹiːt/
*v.* 1. **對待, 處理** — interact in a certain way
*“Do right by her”*
*“Treat him with caution, please”*
2. **治療, 照顧** — provide treatment for
*“The doctor treated my broken leg”*
*“The nurses cared for the bomb victims”*
3. **論述, 涉及, 對付** — act on verbally or in some form of artistic expression
*“This book deals with incest”*
*“The course covered all of Western Civilization”*
4. **宴請, 款待** — provide with a gift or entertainment
*“Grandmother always treated us to the circus”*
*“I like to treat myself to a day at a spa when I am depressed”*
5. *(transitive)* **當 /當, 把……當作 /把……當作, 對待 /對待** — To handle, deal with or behave towards in a specific way.
6. *(transitive)* **請客 /請客** — To entertain with food or drink, especially at one's own expense; to show hospitality to; to pay for as celebration or reward.
*n.* 1. **驚喜 /驚喜** — An unexpected gift, event etc., which provides great pleasure.
2. **樂事** — an occurrence that causes special pleasure or delight
3. something considered choice to eat

*“tempered glass”*

**發音：** /tɹaɪ/
*v.* 1. **探索, 試, 企圖, 試圖, 追求** — make an effort or attempt
*“He tried to shake off his fears”*
*“The infant had essayed a few wobbly steps”*
2. **化驗, 測試, 試驗, 檢驗** — put to the test, as for its quality, or give experimental use to
*“This approach has been tried with good results”*
*“Test this recipe”*
3. **判決, 宣判, 裁定, 審理** — put on trial or hear a case and sit as the judge at the trial of
*“The football star was tried for the murder of his wife”*
*“The judge tried both father and son in separate trials”*
4. **品嚐, 辨味, 嘗, 嘗味** — take a sample of
*“Try these new crackers”*
*“Sample the regional dishes”*
5. **嘗試 /嘗試, 企圖 /企圖, 試 /試** — To attempt; to endeavour. Followed by infinitive.
6. **審判, 審理, 審訊, 審問** — examine or hear (evidence or a case) by judicial process
*“The jury had heard all the evidence”*
*“The case will be tried in California”*
*n.* 1. **力圖, 努力, 盡力, 嘗試** — earnest and conscientious activity intended to do or accomplish something
*“made an effort to cover all the reading material”*
*“wished him luck in his endeavor”*

<a id="entry-t-004031"></a>
## try on

*v.* 1. *(transitive)* **試穿 /試穿** — To test the look or fit of (a garment) by wearing it.
2. put on a garment in order to see whether it fits and looks nice
*“Try on this sweater to see how it looks”*

## tube

**發音：** /tuːb/
*n.* 1. **筒, 管, 管子, 管狀** — a hollow cylindrical shape
2. **筒** — An approximately cylindrical container, usually with a crimped end and a screw top, used to contain and dispense semiliquid substances.
3. **管狀結構, 管狀部分** — (anatomy) any hollow cylindrical body structure
4. **地下鐵路, 地下鐵道, 地鐵** — an electric railway operating below the surface of the ground (usually in a city)
*“in Paris the subway system is called the `metro' and in London it is called the `tube' or the `underground'”*
5. conduit consisting of a long hollow object (usually cylindrical) used to hold and conduct objects or liquids or gases
6. electronic device consisting of a system of electrodes arranged in an evacuated glass or metal envelope
*v.* 1. **提供管子, 插入管道** — provide with a tube or insert a tube into
2. convey in a tube
*“inside Paris, they used to tube mail”*
3. ride or float on an inflated tube
*“We tubed down the river on a hot summer day”*
4. place or enclose in a tube

*n.* 1. **錯字 /錯字, 訛字 /訛字, 手民之誤 /手民之誤, 誤排 /誤排, 印錯 /印錯, 別字 /別字, 錯別字 /錯別字, 誤植 /誤植, 筆誤 /筆誤** — A typographical error.
2. a mistake in printed matter resulting from mechanical failures of some kind
*v.* 1. *(transitive)* **誤植 /誤植, 打錯 /打錯, 打錯字 /打錯字** — To make a typographical error.

## typography

**發音：** /taɪˈpɒɡɹəfi/
*n.* 1. *(uncountable, usually)* **字體排印學 /字體排印學** — The art or practice of setting and arranging type; typesetting.

<a id="entry-t-004602"></a>
## typology

**發音：** /taɪˈpɒl.ə.d͡ʒi/
*n.* 1. *(countable, uncountable)* **類型學 /類型學** — The systematic classification of the types of something according to their common characteristics.
2. *(countable, uncountable)* **語言類型學 /語言類型學** — Classification of languages according to their linguistic trait (as opposed to ancestrality like Romance languages).
3. classification according to general type

<a id="entry-t-004603"></a>
## tyrannical

*adj.* 1. **壓制+的, 壓制性+的, 壓迫的, 殘暴的, 暴虐+的** — marked by unjust severity or arbitrary behavior
*“the oppressive government”*
*“oppressive laws”*

*“autocratic government”*

<a id="entry-t-004604"></a>

*v.* 1. **施行暴政, 施行虐政, 壓迫** — rule a country as a tyrant

*“her husband and mother-in-law tyrannize her”*

<a id="entry-t-004605"></a>
## tyrannize

**發音：** /ˈtɪɹ.ən.aɪz/

## tyrannosaur

2. large carnivorous bipedal dinosaur having enormous teeth with knifelike serrations; may have been a scavenger rather than an active predator; later Cretaceous period in North America

<a id="entry-t-004607"></a>

2. large carnivorous bipedal dinosaur having enormous teeth with knifelike serrations; may have been a scavenger rather than an active predator; later Cretaceous period in North America

<a id="entry-t-004610"></a>
## tyranny

**發音：** /ˈtərəni/
*n.* 1. *(countable, uncountable)* **僭主政治, 獨裁 /獨裁, 暴政, 暴戾** — A government in which a single ruler (a tyrant) has absolute power, or this system of government; especially, one that acts cruelly and unjustly.
2. **專制政治, 專制政治論, 僭主政治, 暴政** — dominance through threat of punishment and violence
3. *(countable, uncountable)* **極權 /極權** — Absolute power, or its use.
4. a form of government in which the ruler is an absolute dictator (not restricted by a constitution or laws or opposition etc.)

<a id="entry-t-004611"></a>
## tyrant

**發音：** /ˈtaɪɹənt/
*n.* 1. **暴君, 暴主, 桀紂 /桀紂** — A despot; a ruler who governs unjustly, cruelly, or harshly.
2. a cruel and oppressive dictator
3. in ancient Greece, a ruler who had seized power without legal right to it
4. any person who exercises power in a cruel way
*“his father was a tyrant”*

<a id="entry-t-004612"></a>

*n.* 1. **霸鶲 /霸鶲** — Any of a group of passerine birds, of family Tyrannidae, that inhabit the Americas.
